Only exact capability/profile combinations with their required evidence are qualified; successful operation does not promote support.

The ordinary device-allocation minimum-alignment projection applies only to ordinary base allocations; it adds no caller-selected alignment, arbitrary offset-view guarantee, native support promotion, or performance claim.

SPEC-0010 relocatable PTX and SPEC-0012 Device LTO have exact Windows native qualification; Linux and every other provider/device profile remain independently gated. SPEC-0011 u64/i32/f32 scalar launch kinds retain their own native promotion gate.
SPEC-0021 f64/f16/bf16 scalar launch kinds are implemented in the public portable/software/package path; their exact native ABI/launch promotion evidence remains open.

SPEC-0021 contiguous one-dimensional typed device views are implemented as allocation-owned opaque public capabilities with explicit launch-access enforcement. Portable/package behavior is implemented; native view consumption remains unqualified.

SPEC-0016 opaque GPU operation submission/completion has exact Windows delayed-completion/deferred-failure/cleanup evidence only for its recorded Node/Driver/GPU profile; no broader support is implied.

SPEC-0018 capacity-two scheduling and SPEC-0019 internal-pinned async transfers have exact Windows and installed-package evidence only for the recorded Node/Driver/GPU profile; the compatibility default remains one pending operation.

SPEC-0014 publication mailboxes have exact Windows and installed-package evidence only for privately mapped named u32 lanes, one live GPU operation lease, and system-scope acquire/release publication on the recorded Node/Driver/GPU profile.

SPEC-0013 Device-JS plus the scoped atomic-observation and device-publication children is an implemented restricted frontend using pinned Acorn only for syntax parsing; exact Windows source-only generated-source/compiler/launch/oracle/lifecycle evidence qualifies only its recorded profile.

inspectDeviceProgram() is a pure CUDA-free frontend inspection path. Its portable/package conformance proves only deterministic Device-JS semantic validation and public descriptor projection; it does not claim native/provider execution or performance.

SPEC-0030 adds an exact additive Device-JS dense numeric profile for f64/f16/bf16 pointers, locals, device functions, kernel scalars, casts, arithmetic and special-value math. Exact installed-package Windows CUDA 13.3 header/compiler/compute_75/GTX 1660 Ti numerical-oracle and cleanup evidence does not qualify Linux, other providers/targets, tensor operations, tensor cores, fast math, or performance.

SPEC-0030-erf-v1 additively admits same-kind f32/f64 gpu.math.erf through the dense numeric profile and private ordinary erff/erf lowering. Portable/package evidence does not promote native numerical accuracy, provider compatibility, Linux support, fast-math, lower precision, GELU semantics, or performance.

SPEC-0030-tanh-v1 additively admits same-kind f32/f64 gpu.math.tanh through the dense numeric profile and private ordinary tanhf/tanh lowering, with canonical composition after erf when both children are required. Portable/package evidence does not promote native numerical accuracy, provider compatibility, Linux support, fast-math, lower precision, activation/model semantics, or performance.

SPEC-0022 device publication has exact Windows installed-package evidence only for naturally aligned u32/u64 device-scope release/acquire readiness and one immutable multiword payload on the recorded profile; freshness, progress, generation policy and queue correctness remain excluded.

SPEC-0017 device selection is implemented in the portable/software/package path. Default-device compatibility and explicit selector orchestration are mock-qualified only; native default/explicit selection and distinct-device behavior remain unqualified until exact independent evidence exists.

SPEC-0020 immutable prepared operation DAGs implement canonical kernel-only identity plus the bounded SPEC-0031 cuBLASLt f32 child, replay, one whole-DAG operation lifecycle, derived library accesses, and a single-stream semantic realization. Exact installed-package Windows native preparation, mixed kernel/library submission, result parity, and cleanup evidence qualifies only the recorded profile. CUDA Graph realization and performance benefit remain unimplemented or unqualified.

SPEC-0023 and SPEC-0029 implement one optional context-owned cuBLASLt f32 row-major matmul profile over typed views and the ordinary operation lifecycle. Exact Windows CUDA 13.3 / cuBLASLt 13.5.1 ABI, numerical, public lifecycle, provider identity, and cleanup evidence does not qualify Linux, other provider versions, other dtypes/layouts, or performance.
Linux package import, source admission, readiness, and portable testing are not native CUDA support; WSL remains backend-unavailable.

This bundle qualifies only the exact source/runtime/provider/device tuple recorded above; it does not promote another OS, GPU, driver, toolkit, Node, target, or CUDA-JS revision.

The recorder uses only the public cuda-js package and public capability methods; no generated CUDA/PTX, raw handle, pointer, FFI, or private CUDA-JS surface is inspected by CUDA-MCGS.
